PC: Patient Introduction: Inaccurate , incomplete, and/or includes excessive irrelevant data
Patient Introduction: Accurate with most of the pertinent information included and most of the irrelevant data omitted
Patient Introduction: Concise and comprehensive
History of Present Illness: Inaccurate , incomplete, and/or includes excessive irrelevant data
History of Present Illness: Accurate, mostly organized sequence of relevant events with well-characterized symptoms (quality, severity, etc.) and most of the irrelevant data omitted
History of Present Illness: Hypothesis (assessment) driven, concise, comprehensive, organized. Includes PMH, FH, SH elements directly relevant to the differential and collateral history if indicated.
Additional History: Past Medical History, Family History, Social History, Review of Systems: Inaccurate, incomplete, and/or poorly described
Additional History: Past Medical History, Family History, Social History, Review of Systems: Accurate, complete, age-appropriate PMH, FH, SH, and ROS

Additional History: Past Medical History, Family History, Social History, Review of Systems: Patient specific. Eg: developmental/nutritional screening; HEADSS for adolescents; seasonal influenza vaccine; close contact Tdap for infants, etc.
Vital Signs and Growth Parameters: Inaccurate and/or incomplete
Vital Signs and Growth Parameters: Accurate with complete vital signs and some  age-appropriate growth parameters/percentiles (minimum wt and percentile)

Vital Signs and Growth Parameters: All age-appropriate growth parameters/percentiles. Patient specific. Eg: preemie/syndrome specific growth chart; wt for length %; prior growth pattern; orthostatics; pain scale, etc. when appropriate
Physical Exam: Inaccurate and/or incomplete
Physical Exam: Accurate, complete, age-appropriate physical exam with some expanded focus based on presenting symptoms.

Physical Exam: Hypothesis (assessment) driven. When appropriate, includes subtle positive and negative findings, comparison with past exams, and/or additional maneuvers that distinguish among diagnoses under consideration. Eg: dentition with suspected bulimia; acanthosis nigricans; comparison with prior liver size; psoas sign, etc.
Diagnostic Studies: Inaccurate, incomplete, and/or transcribed without appropriate attribution
Diagnostic Studies: Accurately reports pertinent positive and negative studies while omitting most of the irrelevant data
Plan: Poorly described, unsupported, and/or does not match the problem list or assessment
Plan: Addresses most aspects of the identified problems while describing decision making rationale. Includes patient/caregiver education and discharge/follow-up plans when appropriate.

Plan: Accurately, concisely, and thoroughly addresses all identified problems. Considers patient/caregiver preferences, literature/practice guidelines, cost effectiveness, and/or contingency plans when appropriate.
MK: Diagnostic Studies: Accurately interprets pertinent positive and negative studies. When appropriate, includes review of prior studies, age/gender norms, calculations, and/or own review of diagnostic imaging. Eg: maternal labs; prior HbA1C; prior ejection fraction; Hb mean for age/gender; anion gap; Na correction for glu, etc.
Problem Identification: Absent, inaccurate, splits/joins problems inappropriately, and/or confuses systems and problems
Problem Identification: Accurately identifies primary hospital problem/s at highest diagnostic level based on available information

Problem Identification: Accurately prioritizesall active problems identified through history, physical exam, and diagnostic studies including secondary problems that should be addressed during hospitalization. Eg: second hand smoke exposure; underimmunized status; developmental delay; obesity; anemia, etc.

Assessment: Absent, unsupported, misses many critical findings, includes excessive irrelevant data, fails to include physical exam/diagnostic study findings, and/or restates findings without synthesis

Assessment: Identifies some defining history AND physical exam/diagnostic study findings while omitting mostof the irrelevant data. Uses some medical terms and semantic qualifiers to synthesize an assessment.

Assessment: Selects critical defining history ANDphysical exam/diagnostic study findings. Uses appropriate medical terms and semantic qualifiers to synthesize an accurate and concise summary statement.
Differential Diagnosis: Absent, unsupported, and/or poorly described
Differential Diagnosis: Includes a prioritized differential while committing to a working diagnosis. Supports clinical reasoning with relevant history, physical exam, and diagnostic study elements.

Differential Diagnosis: Presents an accurate and concise differential by comparing/contrasting discriminating features of diagnoses under consideration. Includes a differential for secondary problem/s and/or refers to literature when appropriate.
